summary.text: Mike Jones is the Democratic candidate for the Iowa House of Representatives, District 32, in the November 3, 2026 general election, in a race with no incumbent in which no other candidate is listed.
An assistant public defender who says he is the mayor of Windsor Heights, he is running on criminal justice reform, public education and water quality.

paragraphs.text: Mike Jones graduated from Johnston High School, earned a bachelor's degree from the University of Iowa in 2008, and received a law degree from Drake University Law School in 2011.
His listed profession is assistant public defender.
In a Ballotpedia survey, he said he has been a public servant for almost a decade, is currently the Mayor of Windsor Heights, and works as a public defender for the State of Iowa.
Jones advanced from the Democratic primary on June 2, 2026.

In the survey, he said his priorities include criminal justice reform and a path to marijuana legalization, higher pay for public school teachers and an end to the state's education savings account program, and cleaning up water through regulation and penalties for polluters.
He listed the Iowa State Education Association, AFSCME, the Iowa AFL-CIO, Planned Parenthood Advocates of Iowa and the Sierra Club of Iowa among his endorsers.
